title: Joseph, the Fish and the Pearl
summary: Joseph loves Shabbat, and every Friday he buys only the very best at the market in its honor. His rich neighbor is afraid that one day all his gold will pass to Joseph, so he sells everything and buys a single pearl, but the wind blows it into the sea and a fish swallows it. Who will buy that fish at the very last moment on Friday? A rhyming story with a refrain that's fun to sing, based on the Talmudic legend of Joseph Who Honored Shabbat.
pages:
Joseph wore a kippah, round and blue,
And he loved Shabbat with a love so true.
Every Friday he ran to the market, again, with zest,
Calling, "For Shabbat — only the very best!"

He bought a fat fish and golden challot,
White candles too, and good things — a lot!
The merchant said, "Pricey!" and Joseph answered, as he always professed:
"For Shabbat — only the very best!"

In the house next door lived a neighbor who saved and saved.
A wise man told him, "In the end, it will all go to Joseph — all the gold that you craved!"
The neighbor jumped up: "No! He won't take a thing from me!
I'll sell it all and buy just one, and guard it so it can't flee!"

He sold his house, and his horse, and his cart as well,
And bought one pearl — enormous and grand, you could tell.
He put it in his hat and went out onto the bridge,
And said, "Now everything's fine, fine, fine — right up to the ridge!"

Suddenly a wind came, strong as an ox — WHOOSH!
The hat flew off, and the pearl? SPLOOSH!
It dove into the sea, deep, deep, deep,
And a fish opened its mouth... GULP! — swallowed it, and didn't make a peep.

In the morning a fisherman came and spread a giant net,
And caught the fish — what a real find, the best one yet!
The fisherman asked, "Who'll buy? Who?" and nobody would try,
Until someone said, "Go to Joseph! He always will buy."

The sun was already setting, the market almost bare,
And Joseph came running, fast as lightning through the air.
He looked at the fish and said, "Here it is, just as I've always professed:
For Shabbat — only the very best!"

Joseph opened the fish, and inside something gleamed!
He looked, and he looked, and his happy heart leaped and beamed.
An enormous pearl, like a little moon from the sky,
Joseph laughed and danced with all the children, jumping high.

After Shabbat he sold the pearl and got gold in return,
And Joseph? Stayed the same Joseph, who loved Shabbat at every turn.
He invited all his friends to his table to share,
With fish and more fish, and with songs in the air.

And next Friday at the market, among the stalls in a row,
Joseph bought challot and fish and pomegranates aglow.
The merchant asked, "Today too — only the best?"
And Joseph laughed, "As always, again, with zest:
For Shabbat — only the very best!"
